headline: Amazon Web Services' chief executive says data centers use less water than critics claim and that AWS has dropped nondisclosure agreements with officials.
score_reason: Pool 5 kept: a major company's public rebuttal in an active political fight, but the claims are its own and the post is three days old.
importance_line: Residents, local officials and moratorium backers are affected, since the claims are Amazon's own and critics say they leave out water used to make power and chips.
summary: TechCrunch reports that Amazon Web Services chief executive Matt Garman, in a blog post on 2 Oct 2026, said AWS no longer uses nondisclosure agreements with government agencies on data center projects, and argued that four 'myths' about data centers are wrong, including that their direct water use is only 0.5% of US industrial water use. TechCrunch notes these are Amazon's own claims, and that critics say they leave out the water used to generate electricity and make chips.
notes: Follows Amazon's $1 billion community pledge of 2 Oct 2026, which the pool carried on 3 Oct. Pool source was the Times of India; credit moved to TechCrunch, which read the post.
